Subject: Follow-up: Deployment mode & compliance next steps

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today — great to meet you and Michael. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Call recap (30m):
- BrightCare goal: embed clinical summarization and routing in the care coordination flow (PHI in transit and at rest).
- Primary compliance ask: HIPAA coverage + signed BAA, plus SOC 2 Type II evidence for our InfoSec review.
- Deployment considerations discussed: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools, data isolation), Private (VPC/on-prem for strict audit controls).

Initial qualification follow-ups (we're trying to align recommended deployment mode):
1) Will you be sending PHI to Redwood as part of inference requests, or will you route only de-identified data? (short answer: PHI yes/no)
2) Approx expected throughput: peak concurrent requests / tokens per month?
3) Retention & audit needs: do you need per-request logs retained for >12 months, and are audit exports required for SOC/HIPAA audits?
4) Do you require customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) or is platform-managed KMS acceptable?

What we can action immediately:
- I'm attaching our SOC 2 Type II report and a draft BAA for review (see attachments).
- Dev will follow up with recommended deployment modes based on your answer to Q1–Q4 and rough throughput.
- If InfoSec wants a deeper session, we can schedule a security deep-dive next week with our RF and infra leads.

Proposed next steps:
- Sarah: reply with Q1–Q4 (short bullets).
- We'll propose a recommended deployment (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) and a ballpark SOW/pricing.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear notes and the SOC 2 doc. Answers to your questions below: 

1) PHI: Yes, the inference requests will include PHI (patient names, notes, limited identifiers) — we need full HIPAA coverage and a signed BAA.
2) Throughput: Initial pilot ~50 reqs/minute peak, ~2M tokens/month. Production (Q3) could scale to ~300 reqs/minute and ~20M tokens/month.
3) Retention & audit: We need per-request audit logs retained for 24 months and the ability to export logs for audits.
4) Keys: We prefer customer-managed KMS (we use AWS KMS CMKs) but can accept platform-managed if the key separation controls are documented.

Initial ask from InfoSec: please confirm whether Dedicated capacity with VPC peering would meet our requirements, or whether BrightCare would need a Private VPC/private deployment for full compliance posture. Also, please share any architecture notes on how PHI is isolated and encrypted in transit + at rest.

Can you also send a ballpark pricing estimate for Dedicated capacity vs Private deployment (per-month committed vs one-time setup) so we can scope budget?

Happy to schedule an InfoSec call next Wed/Thu afternoon PST if that works for Redwood.

Thanks,
Sarah Thompson
Director, Security & Compliance | BrightCare Health

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the quick answers — helpful. Short technical clarifications and an initial recommendation based on the pilot/production numbers you shared: 

Recommendation (high level):
- Pilot (50 reqs/min, ~2M tokens/month): Hosted API with a BAA could be acceptable if you accept platform-managed KMS and shorter retention.
- Production (300 reqs/min, ~20M tokens/month) with 24mo audit retention & customer-managed KMS: we recommend Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) in a Private VPC configuration. Practically that means Dedicated capacity with VPC peering and optional customer-managed KMS — this delivers isolation, predictable throughput, and supports audit exports.
- If BrightCare requires full on-prem or air-gapped control for keys/audit (e.g., HSM on-prem or separate network fabric), then Private deployment (customer-managed control plane or on-prem package) is the path.

Technical notes on PHI handling: 
- Inference path: requests arrive over TLS to regional ingress -> routed to Dedicated pool (if configured) -> inference runtime executes on isolated GPU nodes -> response returned. 
- Data at rest: model KV caches and any optional persistent logs are encrypted at rest using KMS. We support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS CMKs) for Dedicated / Private deployments; for Hosted, platform-managed KMS is default but customer-managed can be enabled for Dedicated.
- Audit logs: we can export per-request logs (metadata + token counts + timestamps, not full model weights) to your S3 with lifecycle policies; retention configurable up to multi-year. Exports are available for Dedicated and Private.
- SOC2/HIPAA controls: SOC 2 Type II report attached. For HIPAA, we sign a BAA and can add technical addenda about data segmentation and logging.

Attachments in this thread: Redwood-SOC2-TypeII-2025.pdf, Redwood-BAA-draft.docx (draft BAA for review).

Questions for BrightCare to finalize recommendation: 
- Which AWS region(s) will you require for data residency? (us-west-2, us-east-1, etc.)
- Any required approval timeline for pilot -> prod (target date)?
- Do you require HSM-level key custody or will KMS CMKs suffice?

I can pull together a short SOW and ballpark pricing (Dedicated reserved per-GPU/hour + ingress/network fees; Private has a one-time setup & license line) once we confirm region and key custody. Happy to join the InfoSec call next Wed/Thu.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwoodinference.com

Thanks — that recommendation makes sense. A few clarifications before we lock on Dedicated with VPC peering: 

- Region: US-West (us-west-2) required for data residency.
- KMS: CMK acceptable if we can manage the key material in our AWS account (want key rotation policy & proof of separation).
- Audit exports: we want automated daily exports to our S3 with MFA-delete enabled and the ability to produce audit artifacts within 48 hours for regulators.

Next steps from our side: schedule an InfoSec deep-dive (security architecture + compliance) — attendees: myself, Michael Lee (IT Ops), and our procurement lead. Prefer Wed 2026-02-25 10:00–11:00 PST or Thu 2026-02-26 1:00–2:00 PST.

Also: please send a short pricing sketch (monthly committed for Dedicated, and a one-time setup + license range for Private) so procurement can put together a budgetary approval.

Thanks,
Sarah
